short_description: Construction runtime recovery, late-interest synchronization and replication-scale policy over accepted T1A.6 runtime networking.
purpose: Make canonical Construction runtime survive recovery/reconnect and replicate only relevant runtime state at scale while reusing existing persistence, authority and interest foundations instead of creating domain-private global infrastructure.
expected_outcome: Recovered runtime state preserves canonical revisions and effects, reconnect/late-interest clients converge from authoritative baselines, irrelevant constructs are not replicated, and scale behavior is bounded without changing permanent identity or authority ownership.
progress_note: T1A.6 is accepted after transactional-effects FIX1 and fresh Windows focused/full regression. T1A.7 is opened for architecture/reuse audit before runtime implementation; MW7 interest/reconnect and existing persistence repository/coordinator boundaries are being treated as watched dependencies, not copied foundations.
next_stage: Complete architecture/reuse audit, then implement the smallest recovery + late-interest + selective-replication candidate and focused acceptance.

ownership_claims.scope: canonical Construction runtime recovery projection and domain runtime state
consume existing transport/session/channel policy; T1A.7 may add domain projection adapters only
consume existing durable repository/coordinator semantics; no private T1 durability model
consume authority_epoch/session fences; no new permanent owner registry
